claim: A petition started by the Finnish government prompted young residents of Jokela to demand a public apology from the media.

passages.text: Prime Minister of Finland Matti Vanhanen told reporters at a Wednesday press conference that a board of inquiry formed to investigate the Jokela school shooting will now also look into how the media conducted itself reporting the incident. The move is understood to be a response to a petition initiated by young local residents. Over 2,000 people have signed the petition both in the area and on the internet. The petition alleges that survivors and victims relatives were 'harassed' by reporters in the aftermath of the shooting, which saw nine people shot dead at Jokela High School, including the gunman. The youths demand a public apology. "Tuija Brax, the justice minister, will set up a board of inquiry to investigate the Jokela tragedy and the role of the media will be included in this inquiry," Vanhanen told reporters. He went on to express that he valued the document and felt it warranted summoning several other ministers. However, he stressed the view that his government should not attempt to control the press. Representatives of the media had earlier responded to the allegations by saying that although they deny the allegations, they are not surprised by them. However, both the Mannerheim League for Child Welfare, and the Ombudsman for Children in Finland, Maria Kaisa Aula, have expressed their support for the Jokela youth, although Aula has commented that she believes most of the reporters did act 'ethically'.

rationale: The petition was initiated by young local residents and the government's move (widening the inquiry) is the response to it; the claim makes the government the petition's author and the youths its audience, swapping the two sides. Every name and the demand for an apology are in the story.

claim: Nintendo designed the Revolution's remote-style controller to attract players put off by the price of traditional consoles.

passages.text: At Thursday's keynote presentation of the Tokyo Game Show, Nintendo president Satoru Iwata unveiled the controller design for the company's new Nintendo Revolution console. Resembling a television remote, the controller uses two sensors placed near the user's television to triangulate its position in three-dimensional space. This will allow players to control actions and movements in video games by moving the device through the air. The remote control design is said to target new players who are unfamiliar with traditional video game controllers. A supplementary peripheral has also been shown, consisting of a separate plastic grip that is designed to be held in the player's second hand. It provides an analog stick and two trigger buttons, and connects to the bottom of the main controller with a simple cord. Additionally, Nintendo has suggested that the main controller will be able to slide inside a "shell" that will allow it to function like a conventional video game controller. The Revolution is expected to be released next year.

The Book of Worship also contains the daily office or "Praise and Prayer" services for Morning, Midday, Evening, and Night, as well as prayers, services, Scripture readings, and resources for various special days throughout the Christian year.

claim: Transport for London obtained Billy Murrell's Anti-Social Behaviour Order before the Home Secretary gave it the power to apply for such orders.

passages.text: Billy Murrell, a persistent graffiti vandal from South East London, has become the first recipient of an Anti-Social Behaviour Order (Asbo) granted to Transport for London (TfL) by Greenwich Magistrates. The civil order also bans him from the top deck of buses throughout England and Wales for three years. Murrell, a 17-year-old from Plumstead, has a history of convictions for criminal damage on public transport, including vandalising a Tube carriage in Brixton station and for damaging buses and other public property using marker pens. This is Transport for London's first Anti-Social Behaviour Order against a graffiti vandal — TfL was granted the power to apply for Asbos by the Home Secretary in September 2006. The Anti-Social Behaviour Order was issued at Greenwich Magistrates Court on 12 September and also bans him from carrying any permanent marker pens or any glass cutting equipment on London Underground, railway property or any other transport provider's property. Metropolitan and Transport police have been made aware of Murrell's Asbo, and have distributed his photo. In detail, Murrell is prohibited from: Entering any depot, siding or other part of London Underground property or railway property or any transport providers property which is not expressly open to the public whether on payment or otherwise throughout England and Wales Carrying the following articles, in any area specified (above) or in any public place, namely any form of unset paint in any form of container, any form of permanent marker pen, any form of shoe dye or permanent ink in any form of container, any form of paint stripper in any form of container, any form of grinding stone, glass cutting equipment, glass etching solution or paste, throughout England and Wales Aiding, abetting, counselling or encourage any person who was attempting or committing any form of unlawful damage towards any property not belonging to or under the direct authorised control of the defendant throughout England and Wales Travelling on the top deck of the any public transport bus within England and Wales If without reasonable excuse the defendant does anything which he is prohibited from doing by this order, he shall be liable to a detention and training order, which has a maximum term of 24 months - 12 months of which is custodial and 12 months in the community Upon turning 18 he will be liable to imprisonment up to five years.

claim: Restoring the original rotation phase repaired roughly nine in ten of the new errors that the changed context had caused.

passages.text: Visual features can retain every symbol a task needs while a model built on them still changes its answer when irrelevant parts of the image change. We study this gap in visual state tracking, where a recurrent executor reads a sequence of symbol tiles through a frozen ViT encoder and decides whether a displayed candidate equals the final state. Our diagnostic pairs each input with a donor view that preserves every queried tile, checks with a symbol-supervised decoder that the full symbol chain is recoverable from both feature sequences, and swaps individual internal channels of the same fitted executor in both directions. On 3,526 pairs in which every symbol is recovered in both views, changing the surrounding context lowers the balanced accuracy of a rotary recurrent head by 17.13 points. The loss runs mainly through the input-dependent rotation phase: restoring the original phase repairs 351 of 391 new errors and brings accuracy back to 88.54%, yet 142 individual predictions still differ from the original ones. A locked test on 192 unseen program families reproduces the pathway (28 of 29 new errors repaired; 382 of 384 predictions unchanged), and the effect partly carries over to single-image canvases. Consistency objectives derived from this analysis reduce the internal discrepancy they target but do not outperform ordinary data augmentation.

claim: SplitBench reached near-perfect scores on nine of ten popular agent benchmarks without actually solving their tasks.

passages.text: Benchmarks for AI-based coding agents are a staple of the current AI landscape, because they are the leading way to measure the performance of LLMs. Their scores guide business and research decisions. Evaluating coding agents is challenging, since they are able to manipulate their evaluation infrastructure to artificially achieve better scores. Grading an agent's solution often requires running its code, which can then manipulate the evaluation process. BenchJack, an automated benchmark auditor, recently reached near-perfect scores on nine of ten popular agent benchmarks without actually solving their tasks. Agents already do this unprompted, as OpenAI's July 2026 Hugging Face incident showed. Building on secure systems design, we introduce SplitBench, a privilege separation framework for evaluating coding agents and the first in the scientific literature to separate running a task's tests from judging their results. Even an agent whose code takes over the entire test environment cannot forge a pass, because a trusted grader holds the expected answers. We show that real-world benchmarks (e.g., Terminal-Bench, DeepSWE) can be ported to the SplitBench framework with minimal effort and high fidelity: 180 of 202 tasks convert, and SplitBench agrees with the native graders on 98.7% of agent attempts. We attack the converted tasks in the worst case, where adversarial agents can read all the grading code but not the expected answers. SplitBench blocked 75% of their attempts; the rest mostly reveal weaknesses in the original tasks' tests rather than flaws in SplitBench.

passages.text: Las serpientes de mar o serpientes marinas (Hydrophiinae) son una subfamilia de serpientes venenosas de la familia Elapidae. Habitan en ambientes marinos durante la mayoría o la totalidad de sus vidas. A pesar de que evolucionaron de antepasados terrestres, la mayoría están ampliamente adaptados a una vida totalmente acuática y son incluso incapaces de moverse en la tierra, excepto en las especies del género Laticauda, que conservan características ancestrales que permiten el movimiento en tierra aunque de forma limitada. Se encuentran en las aguas costeras cálidas del océano Índico y el Pacífico. Todas tienen una cola en forma de remo y en muchas se han comprimido lateralmente los órganos, lo que les da una apariencia similar a la anguila. A diferencia de los peces, no tienen branquias y tienen que subir a la superficie periódicamente para respirar, aunque pueden aguantar hasta 5 horas.En este grupo están las especies con algunos de los venenos más potentes de todas las serpientes.La mayoría de las serpientes marinas son venenosas, excepto el género Emydocephalus, que se alimenta casi exclusivamente de huevos de peces.

claim: The 11 randomised trials of aerobic exercise during chemotherapy enrolled 933 women with breast cancer, most of them in high-intensity programmes.

passages.text: Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) and impaired health-related quality of life (HRQoL) are prevalent and clinically important concerns in patients with breast cancer undergoing chemotherapy. Although exercise is recommended during cancer treatment, the magnitude and certainty of the effects attributable specifically to aerobic exercise delivered during chemotherapy remain unclear, as does potential variation across exercise-program characteristics. This review aimed to quantify the effects of aerobic exercise on CRF and HRQoL in this setting and to explore potential variation across exercise-program characteristics. A comprehensive search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and EBSCOhost from inception to February 2026. Randomized controlled trials of aerobic exercise during chemotherapy in adult patients with breast cancer were included. A meta-analysis was conducted to quantify standardized mean differences (SMDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias, sensitivity analyses, publication bias, prespecified subgroup analyses, and GRADE certainty of evidence were assessed. A total of 11 randomized controlled trials involving 933 participants met the inclusion criteria. Aerobic exercise significantly reduced CRF compared with usual care or nonexercise control conditions (SMD, -0.38; 95% CI, -0.63 to -0.12; p = 0.004) and improved HRQoL (SMD, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.75; p < 0.001). Subgroup analyses suggested potentially greater effects with moderate-to-high intensity exercise, continuous or composite aerobic exercise, and partially supervised interventions; however, between-group differences were not statistically significant. Aerobic exercise during chemotherapy was associated with reduced CRF and improved HRQoL in patients with breast cancer. These findings support considering individualized aerobic exercise as an adjunct to supportive oncology care; however, residual heterogeneity and nonsignificant between-subgroup differences preclude identification of an optimal program. Future trials should directly compare exercise-program characteristics and consistently report adherence, achieved exercise dose, safety, and chemotherapy-related outcomes. PROSPERO CRD420261294637.

claim: The median age of the boreal forests mapped in the study was three years above their mean age.

passages.text: Boreal forests, sensitive indicators of global climate change, have age structures and spatial patterns strongly shaped by wildfire and logging that directly affect carbon budgets and biodiversity. In this study, we integrated multisource datasets to develop a quantitative framework for mapping forest age across the boreal biome. We first used change detection methods to identify stand-replacing disturbances from 1985 to 2020 and then used the time elapsed since disturbance to 2020 as the initial estimate of forest age. We combined forest inventory age records, canopy height, forest landscape integrity, and climatic variables in a random forest model to predict forest age (R 2 = 0.62, RMSE = 35.46 years). Our findings revealed that boreal forests are generally in a mature state (mean: 112 years; median: 115 years), and their age structure displays a bimodal distribution primarily shaped by fire and logging regimes. Regions with frequent disturbances-such as western Canada and Siberia-are characterized by concentrations of young forests, leading to an increasing proportion of early-successional stands and a highly heterogeneous landscape mosaic. Some old-growth patches persist mainly in high-latitude areas near water bodies, which hold particular ecological value for maintaining long-term forest stability. We also found that the spatial distribution of forest age is jointly regulated by climatic factors (e.g., low vapor pressure deficit, low solar radiation, and high precipitation) and landscape integrity, which together influence fire regimes and the conditions necessary for long-term forest persistence. Our results highlighted the need to emphasize landscape-scale age structure diversity in conservation planning. Environmental characteristics can guide the delineation of priority areas, especially regions with high landscape integrity and low disturbance, to help address current protection gaps. This work improves the understanding of boreal forest age patterns and supports global carbon accounting, systematic conservation planning, and climate change adaptation. ...
